neighbours.label: the word ' baking' as a modifier of a noun (baking spice, baking soda, baking powder), as opposed to baking as a verb and to other ingredients in the same sentences
fire: This red wine shows ripe plum with hints of baking spice on the nose.
Stir a spoonful of baking soda into the warm water.
Sift the flour and the baking powder into a large bowl.
The stout has a sweet finish with light baking spices and dark fruit.
Keep an open box of baking soda in the fridge to absorb smells.
Her recipe calls for two teaspoons of baking powder and some butter.
Oak barrels give this bourbon a warm aroma of baking spice.
A paste of baking soda will clean the burnt pot.
quiet: This red wine shows ripe plum with hints of smoke on the nose.
Stir a spoonful of honey into the warm water.
Sift the flour and the cocoa into a large bowl.

Keep an open bottle of olive oil in the cupboard away from light.

Oak barrels give this bourbon a warm aroma of toffee.
He kept baking until the burnt pot was full.
